domain: History of Mathematics / Philosophy of Mathematics / Epistemology
topic_summary: Analysis of zero's entry into Western mathematics as a number, examining the transition from Indian mathematical innovation through Islamic transmission to European adoption. The topic investigates whether zero's acceptance represents a contested kernel—different readings of what mathematical objects are—or a single constraint (epistemological resistance) observed from different positions.

key_entities: Brahmagupta (7th century Indian mathematician, first to treat zero as number with arithmetic rules)
Aryabhata (5th century Indian mathematician, established zero as digit)
Al-Khwarizmi (9th century Persian mathematician, transmitted Hindu numerals to Islamic world)
Fibonacci (13th century Italian mathematician, introduced Hindu-Arabic system to Europe via Liber Abaci)
Christian theological authorities (associated zero with void/satanic absence)
European merchant class (early adopters for practical calculation)
European learned institutions (monasteries, Medici bank, English Exchequer—late adopters)
key_tensions: Placeholder vs number (Babylonian/Mayan positional notation vs Indian zero-as-quantity)
Practical utility vs philosophical coherence (merchants vs learned circles)
Existence-based ontology vs void-permitting ontology (Greek/Christian vs Indian/Islamic)
Foreign innovation vs institutional conservatism (Hindu-Arabic system vs Roman numerals/abacus)
key_mechanisms: Transmission chain: India (5th-7th c.) → Islamic world (9th c.) → Europe (12th-13th c.)
Dual adoption pathway: merchant class (13th c.) vs institutions (16th c.)
Philosophical gatekeeping: Aristotelian void-rejection + Christian theological resistance
key_absences: No discussion of Chinese mathematical tradition's independent zero development
Limited evidence of specific institutional prohibitions (resistance described as cultural/philosophical rather than legally enforced)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: What mathematical objects are: whether 'number' can denote absence/void or must denote existing quantity
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Philosophical tradition (Aristotelian metaphysics) + theological doctrine (God-in-all-that-exists) grounding what counts as legitimate mathematical entity
commitment_system_recognition.collapse_reason: Initial hypothesis: existence-grounding vs void-permitting readings would emit different constraints (different victim sets, different ε). Actual finding: both readings converge on the SAME constraint—epistemological resistance to zero-as-number—with identical structural delta (philosophical incompatibility with void), identical primary observable (adoption lag), and identical ε bin (low). The 'contest' is not between two readings of what numbers are, but between one reading (existence-grounding) and empirical pressure (practical utility). This is a single constraint observed from different positions (Greek/Christian resistance vs merchant pragmatism), not multiple constraints from one kernel. The M4/M5 seam collapses: there is no interpretive layer here, only one constraint and its eventual abandonment under external pressure.
